views.view_notes: Personally viewed architecture_quantize_grid.png through view_image. I can follow two horizontal rows: 0.7 -> 1.4 -> 1 -> 0.5 and 1.2 -> 2.4 -> 2 -> 1.0. The column labels make division, nearest-integer selection and multiplication explicit. The bottom differences show lost detail of 0.2. All numbers and Chinese text are legible; no overlap, clipping or arrow ambiguity obstructed reading.

Personally viewed architecture_int4_packing.png through view_image. It says storage code = original + 8. In the upper example the first code 0000 follows a green dashed arrow into the right-hand low nibble, while second code 0111 follows the orange arrow into the left-hand high nibble. The crossed arrows are clear because of color, dash pattern and destination labels. I read 0111 0000 -> decimal 112 and the lower 1001 1000 -> decimal 152. The bottom sentence repeats first/right/low and second/left/high. Large legible labels; no obstruction.

Personally viewed capstone_resources.png through view_image. Four expert boxes remain present, with 1 and 3 highlighted and selected by arrows. Boxes 2 and 4 explicitly say they are not used this time but their weights must still be stored. The common-rules box contains the vocabulary table, attention, router and output. The bottom warnings separate all weights, work per token and dispatch cost. I understood this as a storage/computation distinction, with no suggestion that each expert is a full separate model. No layout obstruction.

Personally viewed architecture_distillation_temperature.png through view_image. The three complete probability bars have the same candidate/color order 4,3,5. T=1 is mostly blue (93.62%), T=2 is less concentrated (73.61%,16.43%,9.96%), and T=4 is flatter (54.34%,25.67%,19.99%). Candidate 4 remains largest. The first row rounded labels sum to 99.99%, consistent with the rounding note. The text and bars are legible; no clipping or overlap blocks understanding. This helped interpret p_T and q_T in section 19.10.
